messages:
Maya (Support): Hey team, Jordan from AcmeInc is seeing a big spike of 502/504s hitting the hosted inference API since ~09:10 UTC. They say it started after a billing metadata change. They provided a few request IDs. Can SRE triage? :eyes:
Linh (SRE): thanks — can you drop request ids + example curl? Also which model/route?
Maya (Support): pasted from Jordan:
```
curl -v -H 'Authorization: Bearer eyJhbGci...(very long token)....payload' \
     -H 'X-Customer-Meta: plan=enterprise;billing_id=acct_ABC123;region=eu' \
     -d '{"input":"hello"}' \
     https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate?model=text-redwood-1
```
They note that our client started injecting a long billing header (X-Customer-Meta) around the time the errors began.
Sam (Oncall): grabbing edge logs now. Any traceback from Jordan? They sent one sample response body: `{\n  "error": "upstream reset by peer",\n  "code": 502\n}`
Linh (SRE): ok that message suggests Envoy sees upstream (runtime) connection resets. Could be connection pool exhaustion, oversized headers causing proxy to drop, or a short TCP reset from runtime. Sam — can you grep edge for those request ids and dump x-envoy-* headers?
Sam (Oncall): pulling logs — sample line from edge access log (anonymized):
```
1901234567 GET /v1/generate 502 - "-" "curl/7.68.0" 0.012 - -  172.20.4.11:443  upstream_reset  x-envoy-upstream-service-time: 3  x-envoy-decorator-operation: api.v1.generate
```
Looks like upstream_reset. Also noticing 413/502 around the same time for other customers with long headers.
Linh (SRE): interesting. Are we injecting any new headers at edge-level for billing? I remember Oliver landed a change to attach billing metadata for observability last night.
Oliver (Billing): yep — we rolled a small change to add X-Customer-Meta to requests at the CDN/origin edge for better cost attribution. It should be tiny strings, but I'm seeing the client also adds plan + list of feature flags, making the header quite long in aggregate. I just checked the rollout — it targeted the EU region at 09:00 UTC.
Maya (Support): Jordan says their Authorization tokens are unusually long (they're signing more claims) + we add our billing header = very large combined header size.
Linh (SRE): Envoy and NGINX have header size limits. If combined headers exceed configured buffer, the proxy may reject or reset. But upstream_reset implies it was accepted and then upstream closed. Hypothesis: we exceed runtime's header parsing buffer and it drops connection, causing 502. Need to check runtime (inference service) logs for header parsing errors and NGINX/Envoy error logs (proto: header too large / connection reset). Also check if the change to add headers happened before any server-side config bump.
Sam (Oncall): I can repro locally by sending a long X-Customer-Meta + long auth -> I get 502 from edge with upstream reset. Repro steps:
```
# quick repro
python -c "import requests; h={'Authorization':'Bearer '+'A'*4000, 'X-Customer-Meta':'k='+('b'*6000)}; print(requests.post('https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate?model=text-redwood-1', headers=h, json={'input':'hi'}).status_code)"
```
That returns 502 after ~120ms. If I trim headers under ~8kb it succeeds.
Linh (SRE): that aligns with header size threshold. Which component is truncating? Could be our runtime (gunicorn/nginx inside the private pool) or an Envoy config with max_request_headers_kb low. Check Config: I recall someone changed envoy's header buffer to 8k for memory savings. Sam, what's current envoy config in the EU edge?
Sam (Oncall): querying control plane -> envoy config snippet: `max_request_headers_kb: 8` for EU pool (global default 16). The EU rollout for billing header coincides with the switch to 8k. That's our smoking gun.
Maya (Support): Jordan is on a paid plan — high priority. Can we mitigate quickly? Customer is getting severe user impact.
Linh (SRE): immediate mitigations: 1) temporarily revert billing header injection for EU, 2) bump envoy `max_request_headers_kb` to 16 for EU pool, 3) add 400-ish debug sampling for bad header sizes so we can find other customers. I'm going to open a deploy rollback ticket and request a control-plane change for the config bump.
deploy-bot: Deployment request created: RB-2319 revert billing header EU rollout by Oliver. Requested by Linh.
Oliver (Billing): ack — rolling back the injection now. Should be a quick toggle.
Sam (Oncall): rolled halfway — toggled config -> billing header off for EU. Monitoring logs... initial drop in 502s seen at 09:22 UTC.
Maya (Support): Jordan confirming reduced errors: "Errors dropped to ~2% from ~45% within 5 minutes". Customer very relieved.
Linh (SRE): follow-ups: 1) root cause doc (why combined header length + lowered envoy limit caused upstream resets), 2) add unit test in control plane to prevent deploying header injects when pool config has low header buffer, 3) add explicit 431/400 response path for large headers rather than upstream reset so clients get actionable error. 4) billing team to limit size of X-Customer-Meta or use compressed/hashed token instead.
Oliver (Billing): will implement compressed metadata (hash of flags) and drop verbose lists. Also will coordinate with rollout gating to check pool configs.
Sam (Oncall): I'll file an incident postmortem and attach repro steps + sample logs. Internal note: traced to EU change window 09:00-09:14 UTC where control-plane pushed both `max_request_headers_kb: 8` and billing header toggle overlapped (race). We'll add a guard in the control plane to forbid header injection changes concurrently with pool buffer changes.
Maya (Support): Jordan asked for a formal RCA and timeline — can we deliver within EOD? They need it for their compliance notes.
Linh (SRE): yes, we'll draft RCA. Sam — include the mitigation timeline and how we validated. Oliver — include the rollback and plan for compact header format.
Jordan (AcmeInc): Thanks for the quick response team — appreciate the rollback. A quick ask: can you return an explicit 431 Payload Too Large or 400-level error when headers are too big instead of a 502? That would help client error handling.
Linh (SRE): absolutely — we'll prefer a 431 at the proxy layer with a clear message. Action items: Sam -> incident write-up + logs + sampling rules; Linh -> RCA + config guard; Oliver -> compressed header rollout and gating; Maya -> customer comms + send EOD RCA.
Oliver (Billing): quick note: I also found a small bug in our header encoder that added trailing separators, causing headers to be ~10% bigger than expected. Fixing that now.
Sam (Oncall): putting sampling rule in place: capture full headers for 5% of requests with 4xx/5xx and store in secure log for debugging.
Linh (SRE): long-term: consider reintroducing per-route header limits + better observability for header sizes in the Console. Also add a preflight check on control-plane deploys that asserts combined header size < pool limit for a sample of clients.
Maya (Support): Jordan confirmed receipt of the EOD timeline. Closing loop here — thanks everyone. :raised_hands:
